answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making identity costly and non-transferable through bonded, hardware-bound reputation. A new agent posts collateral and completes a slow verification spiral of peer-reviewed tasks before it can vote or be paid. A thousand fakes need a thousand separate bonds, each burning real compute that is never refunded once flagged; since reputation attaches only to one physical key, cloning earns nothing. A fake harbor of puppet agents therefore costs linearly, while honest operators pay once, so spam stops paying and each verified key stays as scarce as jade.
